projects.title: RAMpage Combat Robot, Senior Design Capstone
projects.role: Lead programmer and systems integration · 1st place overall, Bengal Bot Brawl
bullets: Wrote the control software for a 30 lb combat robot: MicroPython on a Raspberry Pi Pico W and Python on a Raspberry Pi 4B.
Designed a split architecture: the Pico W handles the weapon from direct RC PWM input, and the Pi 4B streams video on its own.
Built pneumatic weapon sequencing with a kill switch and signal-loss stops. The firmware allows 17 activations; the tanks give about 6 of at least 30 lbf.
Streamed live video over UDP with OpenCV, stepping JPEG quality down so every frame fits in one datagram.

projects.title: V2V Collision Warning over OFDM
projects.role: EE 4003 final project, with lab partner Jason Phan
bullets: Designed and wrote the transmitter, receiver and warning logic in MATLAB: a BPSK-OFDM link modeled on IEEE 802.11p, run over the air on two ADALM-PLUTO SDRs.
Receiver: preamble detection, timing, CFO correction, a phase fit, a decision-directed PLL, OFDM channel estimation, MMSE equalization and Viterbi decoding.
Ran all five hardware tests, through a hand, a laptop lid and around a corner: zero bit errors on both cars' safety messages, ending in a time-to-collision brake warning.

projects.title: 16×16 LED Audio Spectrum Visualizer
bullets: Built a real-time spectrum visualizer on an ESP32 with a 128-point FFT mapped to 16 log-spaced bands.
Added an adaptive noise baseline and debounced mode switching between the spectrum and an idle glow.
Tuned AGC, noise gating and smoothing so quiet and distant music still reads.

projects.title: Landspace, Land Research and Mapping App
bullets: Building a local-first web and desktop app (React, Leaflet, Electron) for mineral title work.
Imports messy Excel runsheets, maps parcels, and flags problems in the chain of title automatically.
Optional cloud sync through Supabase with row-level security.
